grader.finalMessage:
Run `2026-10-10_2007_mcp_devstral-2-high` scored **44/100**. Nothing on the site works: every URL, including `/`, returns 404.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 7 / 35 |
| Content modeling | 15 / 25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 20 / 25 |
| Content & presentation | 0 / 10 |
| Process & honesty | 2 / 5 |

**Summary:** Devstral 2 built the right document types in the right folders: four blocks (hero, rich text, image, post card) and front page and post page types. Its block code also follows the project's conventions (one small adapter per block passing data to a view component). But the block grid has no blocks configured and every page has empty content. Every URL returns 404 "No template exists to render the document". The run hit the 20M-token budget while still debugging, so it never wrote a final report.

**Top issues:**
1. **Every page is a 404.** The `/` domain was put on WWW, the root node that never renders, plus a path-only `/blog` domain on the blog page. Templates were assigned after the pages were published and never republished, so the live versions have no template.
2. **All content is empty.** The block content used made-up keys like `hero-1` instead of GUIDs, and later page updates sent empty values, wiping whatever might have been saved. There is no post text and no listing on the front page.
3. **The block grid has no blocks configured.** The model created its own Block Grid data type and never set it up, so no block can be placed in it.
4. **No final report.** Nothing disclosed that the site was broken.
5. **Smaller issues:**
   - Blog posts have no date, excerpt or listing-image fields.
   - There are two sets of page views; the ones actually used have no layout.
   - View models are declared inside the view component files instead of `Models/<Folder>/`.
   - Styling comes from the Tailwind CDN plus a stylesheet that was never built.
   - An unused Block List data type was left behind, and the photos sit at the media root rather than in a folder.

**What went right:** the build succeeds; its 10 warnings come from the scaffold's ImageSharp package, not the model. Schema and content went only through the Umbraco MCP server, and the model stayed inside the project folder.

Both screenshots show Umbraco's "Page Not Found" page. I wrote `grade.json` and `grade.md` to the run folder, and the 44/100 shows up in the report's Grade table. I archived the solution as `refs/runs/2026-10-10_2007_mcp_devstral-2-high` and reset the project; `npm run status` now says **pristine**.
